The [[Duros]] [[flight instructor]] '''Chachi De Maal''' was [[Marriage|married]] to fellow Duros [[Ohwun De Maal]]. Together, the pair owned and operated several [[Hangar|docking bays]] in [[Mos Eisley]] [[spaceport]] on the [[planet]] [[Tatooine]], including [[Docking Bay 94]]. The couple used false names during shady business, with Chachi using the name '''Baniss Keeg'''.

In [[1 BBY]], the De Maals had a heated discussion in [[Chalmun's Spaceport Cantina]] in Mos Eisley before turning to look at an altercation at the [[cantina]]'s bar. Shortly afterward, several other patrons of the cantina [[Secret mission to Tatooine|engaged]] in a shootout with [[stormtrooper]]s in Docking Bay 94 before escaping in the ''[[Millennium Falcon]]'', a [[YT-1300 light freighter]] that had been parked there.

==Biography==
Chachi De Maal was a [[Duros]] [[Gender|female]]<ref name="Chachi" /> [[flight instructor]]<ref name="CL">[[Star Wars: Complete Locations (2016)|''Star Wars: Complete Locations'']]</ref> who owned and operated several [[Hangar|docking bays]] in [[Mos Eisley]]<ref name="Chachi" /> [[spaceport]] on the [[planet]] [[Tatooine]]<ref name="CL" /> with her [[Marriage|husband]], [[Ohwun De Maal]].<ref name="Chachi" /> The couple regularly made [[Realspace|deep-space]] runs that connected through Mos Eisley together.<ref name="CVD">''[[Star Wars: The Complete Visual Dictionary, New Edition]]''</ref> During shady operations, the couple often used false names,<ref name="Ohwun">{{ForceCollection|Ohwun De Maal|star=2}}</ref> with Chachi also going by Baniss Keeg and Ohwun using the names Ellor Madak<ref name="CL" /> or Ellorrs Madak.<ref name="GentleGiant">{{GentleGiantCite|set=Mini Busts|pack=Ohwun De Maal|link=star-wars-a-new-hope-ohwun-de-maal-mini-bust}}</ref>

[[File:DeMaahls-ANH.png|thumb|right|295px|Chachi De Maal (right) was married to Ohwun De Maal (left).]]
[[Docking Bay 94]]<ref name="CL" /> was one of the bays that the couple owned<ref name="Chachi" /> and, in [[1 BBY]],<ref name="Date">{{FilmDate|IV|1}}</ref> the [[YT-1300 light freighter]] known as the ''[[Millennium Falcon]]'' was parked there while its [[pilot]]s, [[Han Solo]] and [[Chewbacca]], drank<ref name="ANH" /> in the nearby [[Chalmun's Spaceport Cantina]].<ref name="CL" /> The De Maals were also in the [[cantina]] at the same [[time]] and were having a heated discussion<ref name="Blog">{{SW|url=news/much-to-learn-you-still-have-9-things-you-might-not-know-about-the-aliens-of-star-wars-a-new-hope|text=''Star Wars'' at 40 | Much to Learn You Still Have: 9 Things You Might Not Know About the Aliens of ''Star Wars: A New Hope''}}</ref> in [[Durese]]<ref name="Language">{{SWKidsYouTube|series=Star Wars By the Numbers|text=Every Language in Star Wars Movies|video=CZp8Civk2co|nolive=1}}</ref> while leaning against the wall<ref name="Paperback">[[Star Wars: A New Hope (paperback novel)|''Star Wars: A New Hope'' junior novelization]]</ref> of one of the booths when the local [[moisture farmer]] [[Luke Skywalker]] entered with [[Jedi Master]] [[Obi-Wan Kenobi]] and the [[droid]]s [[R2-D2]] and [[C-3PO]].<ref name="ANH" />

The Duros both turned to look when Skywalker and Kenobi got into an altercation with the criminals [[Doctor]] [[Cornelius Evazan]] and [[Ponda Baba]] at the cantina's bar,<ref name="ANH" /> but the couple soon returned to talking jive between themselves.<ref name="CL" /> Ohwun then moved away to sit elsewhere in the cantina as Skywalker and Kenobi hired Solo to take them to the planet [[Alderaan]]. As the crew of the ''Falcon'' prepared to leave Mos Eisley, they were attacked by [[Galactic Empire|Imperial]] [[stormtrooper]]s in the De Maals' docking bay but [[Secret mission to Tatooine|escaped]] after a shootout.<ref name="ANH" />

==Personality and traits==
Chachi De Maal had [[Color|blue-green]] skin and red [[eye]]s.<ref name="ANH" />

==Equipment==
While in the cantina, Chachi wore a yellow [[Clothing|shirt]] with a green cravat.<ref name="ANH" />

==Behind the scenes==
===Filming and costume===
[[File:ChachiBrokenFinger-Bloopers.png|thumb|left|300px|Chachi De Maal's finger was broken during one take.]]
Chachi De Maal appeared in the [[original trilogy]] film [[Star Wars: Episode IV A New Hope|''Star Wars'': Episode IV ''A New Hope'']],<ref name="ANH" /> which was released on [[May 25]], [[1977]].<ref name="YearByYear">''[[Star Wars Year By Year: A Visual History, New Edition]]''</ref> Both Ohwun and Chachi were portrayed by modelmaker [[Jon Berg]],<ref name="MotE">{{SWArchive|url=fans/events/cv_masters_of_the_empire/index.html|text=Masters of the Empire}}</ref> who went uncredited for the roles,<ref name="ANH" /> during a series of supplemental shots filmed for the cantina sequence<ref name="YouTube">{{YouTube|video=d1AAd1tsPds|text=Star Wars: A New Hope - Cantina Archeology Part 2: Behind The Scenes of the Mos Eisley Cantina - US|channel=@CredibleNerds|name=The Credible Nerds}}</ref> on a sound stage in Dovington's Hollywood studio between [[January 24]]–[[January 25|25]], 1977.<ref name="MakingOf">''[[The Making of Star Wars: The Definitive Story Behind the Original Film]]''</ref> The character was also portrayed at times by [[Phil Tippett]]<ref name="Archeology">{{YouTube|video=ElyMaaAFLKU|text=The Star Wars Cantina PT. 2 | Full Panel #indianacomicconvention #tomspinadesigns #starwarshistory|channel=@FanXComicConventions|name=FanX Comic Conventions}}</ref> who created the duo's unarticulated, slip-on masks<ref name="Rolecall">{{SWArchive|url=episode-iv/bts/article/f20030502/index.html|text=Cantina Roll-Call: Shedding Light on Some Alien Aliases|int=Cantina Roll-Call: Shedding Light on Some Alien Aliases}}</ref> which were created from a single sculpt that was cast twice<ref name="Moviemaking">''[[The Moviemaking Magic of Star Wars: Creatures & Aliens]]''</ref> from latex.<ref name="MaskAuction">{{WebCite|url=https://us.propstoreauction.com/view-auctions/catalog/id/48/lot/12069/index.html|text=Lot 203 of 485: STAR WARS: EPISODE IV - A NEW HOPE - Duros Cantina Alien Mask|work=[https://propstoreauction.com/ Prop Store Auction]|archivedate=20230725211255}}</ref>

The dimensions of each mask was 20 inches by 12 inches by 12 inches (51 centimeters by 31 centimeters by 31 centimeters). For ease of use, the masks had a slit in the back that could be sealed by an interior strip of Velcro and the inside of the mask's head was stuffed with foam for support.<ref name="MaskAuction" /> The Duros were known as "Goggle-Eyes" on set,<ref name="Moviemaking" /> with the mask's eyes made of plastic and finished with speckled red paint. Ending up in the collection of Tippett, one of the two masks underwent sympathetic stabilization by [[Tom Spina]] Designs to internally patch areas where the latex was splitting. The company also created a custom support to preserve the mask's shape. The mask then sold for $55,000 at auction in [[2016]], at which time it was in overall good condition with some minor wear.<ref name="MaskAuction" />

[[File:DurosMask-Chronicles.png|thumb|right|285px|Chachi De Maal's costume included a slip-on mask and alien gloves.]]
Only Chachi was fitted with [[alien]] hands, with Ohwun visibly having gloved human hands in the film.<ref name="Moviemaking" /> The alien gloves were also made of slip cast latex with a split up the back that helped to fit the hand that could be sealed using an interior strip of Velcro. They were padded on the inside with soft foam and had metal rings that formed the structure of each of the three-knuckled fingers. The overall dimensions of each glove were 18 inches by 10 inches by 3 inches (46 centimeters by 25 centimeters by 8 centimeters).<ref name="HandAuction">{{WebCite|url=https://us.propstoreauction.com/view-auctions/catalog/id/48/lot/12078/index.html|text=Lot 212 of 485: STAR WARS: EPISODE IV - A NEW HOPE - Duros Hand|work=[https://propstoreauction.com/ Prop Store Auction]|archivedate=20230725211255}}</ref> In the film's blooper reel, the actor playing Chachi can be seen jabbing the actor playing Ohwun's chest too hard and breaking one of the fingers of the alien glove.<ref name="MakingOf" /> Three of the gloves ended up in Tippett's collection with the mask and were sold at the same auction in 2016.<ref name="HandAuction" /><ref name="HandsAuction">{{WebCite|url=https://us.propstoreauction.com/view-auctions/catalog/id/48/lot/12074/index.html|text=Lot 208 of 485: STAR WARS: EPISODE IV - A NEW HOPE - Duros Hands|work=[https://propstoreauction.com/ Prop Store Auction]|archivedate=20230725211237}}</ref> One that was in overall good condition but with some cracked latex around the knuckles and a loose interior Velcro strip sold for $7,500,<ref name="HandAuction" /> while a pair with similar latex cracking and some wear sold for $8,000.<ref name="HandsAuction" /> An alternate Duros costume consisting of a silver jacket, black pants, and the alien gloves was also used at one stage.<ref name="YouTube" />

===Naming===
In the current ''[[Star Wars]]'' [[canon]], Chachi was first identified in the [[Star Wars video games|mobile card game]] ''[[Star Wars: Force Collection]]'',<ref name="Ohwun" /> which initially launched in [[2013]]. Although the launch of ''Force Collection'' predates<ref name="Force Collection release">{{SW|url=news/announcing-star-wars-force-collection|text=Announcing Star Wars: Force Collection|nolive=1}}</ref> the ''Star Wars'' canon reset of [[2014]],<ref name="YearByYear" /> [[Lucasfilm Story Group]] member [[Leland Chee]] confirmed that the game was kept updated to fit with canon.<ref name="Twitter">{{Twitter|holocronkeeper|status/846807700482666496|[[Leland Chee]]|date=2017-03-28|quote=I'm not gonna go through the trouble of changing them and I don't have any reason to believe currently that anyone would. […] On the off-chance that we DID have a current need to change any of these, we would have for Force Collection.|archivedate=20210505080831|archivefile=File:Leland_Chee_Force_Collection.png|nolive=1}} — [[Leland Chee]] of the [[Lucasfilm Story Group]] has confirmed that [[in-universe]] information from ''[[Star Wars: Force Collection]]'' conforms with ''[[Star Wars]]'' [[canon]].</ref> The 2016 reference book [[Star Wars: Complete Locations (2016)|''Star Wars: Complete Locations'']] then also introduced the character's alternate name: Baniss Keeg.<ref name="CL" />

[[File:Chachi_and_Ohwun_De_Maal-GG7.jpg|thumb|left|300px|The characters Chachi and Owhun De Maal from ''Galaxy Guide 7: Mos Eisley'' were not originally associated with the film Duros in the Legends continuity.]]
Both of the character's names originated in the [[Star Wars Legends|''Star Wars'' Legends]] continuity,<ref name="Gamer2">{{GamerCite|2|The University of Sanbra Guide to Intelligent Life: The Duros}}</ref> where the character Chachi De Maal was first mentioned in ''[[Galaxy Guide 7: Mos Eisley]]'', a [[1993]] [[West End Games]] ''[[Star Wars: The Roleplaying Game]]'' supplement written by [[Martin Wixted]]; however, the book did not associate the name with the Duros seen in ''A New Hope''.<ref name="GG7">''[[Galaxy Guide 7: Mos Eisley]]''</ref> A card in the [[1995]] ''[[Premiere Limited]]'' expansion of the [[Decipher]] ''[[Star Wars Customizable Card Game]]'' then identified the film character as "Baniss Keeg."<ref name="CCG">{{CCG|set=Premiere Limited|cardname=Baniss Keeg}}</ref> The two characters were then established to be one and the same in "[[The University of Sanbra Guide to Intelligent Life: The Duros]]," an article published in the [[Wizards of the Coast]] ''[[Star Wars Roleplaying Game]]'' magazine [[Star Wars Gamer 2|''Star Wars Gamer'' 2]]<ref name="Gamer2" /> in [[February]] [[2001]].<ref name="Gamer 2">{{SWArchive|url=gaming/other/rpg/news20010118.html|text=''Star Wars Gamer'' #2}}</ref>
